pattern.description: The whole composition re-lays out: the dashboard card shrinks and slides left while the 'Situation' heading, divider and three bullets slide in together from the right edge, and the blue arc reshapes behind them.
pattern.why_premium: One shared front-loaded ease moves every layer as a single camera-like reframe, making room for the context column without a cut; the bullets are already composed when they arrive, so narration ('Say you're an FP&A director') lands on a finished layout.

build_hint.gsap: tl.to('.dashboard', {scale: 0.8, xPercent: -8, duration: 0.5, ease: 'expo.out'}).fromTo(['.situation-title', '.situation-rule', '.situation-bullet'], {x: 60}, {x: 0, duration: 0.5, ease: 'expo.out', stagger: 0}, '<').to('.arc', {morphSVG: '#arcB', duration: 0.5, ease: 'expo.out'}, '<'); all layers start together, no stagger.
build_hint.remotion: const p = spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 28, stiffness: 200, mass: 1}}); dashboard scale = interpolate(p,[0,1],[1,0.8]), translateX = interpolate(p,[0,1],[0,-80]); text column translateX = interpolate(p,[0,1],[60,0]); arc path interpolated with the same p. Critically damped, no overshoot.

notes: The text column is already partly visible (clipped at the right edge) in the first frame, so it slides into place rather than appearing; whether bullets have a small stagger cannot be resolved from the filmstrip. Arc 'morph' is approximate (could be a scale/shift of a large circle). camera.move is none, so this is treated as in-frame layout motion.
